independent_solution: Addition needs like quantities: two scalars add only with equal dimensions (mass + time is undefined), so (a) 'any two scalars' fails; likewise (e) 'any two vectors' fails (velocity + force is undefined).
(b) A scalar has no direction, so scalar + vector is undefined even with equal dimensions; (f) a component A_x is a number, not a vector, so A + A_x mixes a scalar with a vector and fails.

(c) Any vector times any scalar is a vector with the product dimension (velocity x time = displacement); (d) any two scalars multiply to a scalar with the product dimension. Both are always meaningful.
Temperature, pressure, time, power, total path length, energy, gravitational potential, coefficient of friction and charge are each fully fixed by a magnitude (with sign) and unit: no direction.
Impulse = F * dt (a vector times a duration) = change in momentum, so it carries the direction of the force: it is the only vector.
(a) False: kinetic energy (scalar) is not conserved in an inelastic collision. (b) False: temperature in deg C or negative work are negative scalars. (c) False: mass is a scalar with dimension [M].
(d) False: temperature varies from point to point in a room. (e) True: a scalar has no direction, so rotating the axes cannot change its value.
